chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn A'sham, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who intends to travel during the month of Ramadan and leaves his home after morning prayer. He said: 'If he is in his home at morning, fasting for that day becomes obligatory upon him, unless he travels after midday (dhalj).'

key_terms.دَلْجَةً: A period of time after midday until sunset

ai.seo_question: When does fasting become obligatory for a traveler in Ramadan if they leave home after dawn?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the obligation of fasting is fixed upon reaching the place of residence at dawn, distinguishing this from the Hanafi view where intention alone suffices. The exception for departing after midday (dhalj) allows the traveler to break the fast, reflecting the Shia principle that the traveler's status is determined by their physical location at the time of the fast's establishment, thereby offering practical flexibility for those who delay their departure.
